title: Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 — blocked by Shader Model 6.7 on d3dmetal (SM 6.8 reached with vkd3d-proton + DXVK)
body: ## Report | Field | Value | |---|---| | **Game or launcher** | Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 | | **Steam AppID** | 2537590 | | **Rating** | 1 — does not launch | | **Renderer** | d3dmetal | | **Chip** | Apple M4 | | **macOS version** | 26.5.2 | | **Engine id** | x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r0 | Highball 0.7.14 · MacBook Mac16,12 · 16 GB unified memory · Steam install. ## Notes Stock d3dmetal: hard block. The game refuses to start with Your graphics card does not support Shader Model 6.7 D3DMetal caps at SM 6.6. I hashed the D3DMetal dylibs shipped by Highball and by CrossOver 26.3 — byte-identical — so switching containers changes nothing here. I then spent a session replacing the translation chain to see whether the 6.7 wall is actually passable on Apple Silicon. Summary below in case it saves someone else the effort, or helps whoever wants to push further. ## Alternate stack: D3D12 -> Vulkan -> Metal Instead of D3D12 -> Metal (D3DMetal), I built vkd3d-proton 3.1.0 as PE with mingw-w64 and dropped d3d12.dll / d3d12core.dll next to the game, plus DXVK 3.1 for dxgi/d3d11. This is what Proton does on Linux, where MSFS 2024 runs fine. **The Shader Model 6.7 wall is passable.** Measured with a small D3D12 probe: SHADER MODEL MAXIMO = 6.8 (0x68) ResourceBindingTier=3 TiledResourcesTier=2 ConservativeRaster=1 This only works with Highball's MoltenVK (1.4.1 / Vulkan 1.4). CrossOver 26.3 ships an older MoltenVK that only exposes Vulkan 1.2, and DXVK requires 1.3 — it bails with "Device does not support Vulkan 1.3". Four blockers had to be cleared, in order: 1. **SM 6.7** — 6 patches to vkd3d-proton relaxing the feature gates for SM 6.7/6.8. One of them is a genuine MSL portability bug, not a relaxation: an atomic applied to a *vector element*, which SPIRV-Cross cannot express in Metal Shading Language. That fix is useful to anyone taking vkd3d-proton to Metal. 2. **Feature level 12_1** — no patch needed, `VKD3D_FEATURE_LEVEL=12_1` already exists. Metal has no conservative rasterization, which FL 12_1 requires. 3. **Wine's dxgi is incompatible with vkd3d-proton.** Wine asks for `IWineDXGISwapChainFactory`; vkd3d-proton implements `IDXGIVkSwapChainFactory`, which is what DXVK's dxgi queries. Without DXVK's dxgi the game null-derefs right after shader compilation. Building DXVK then surfaced that DXVK rejects Apple GPUs outright: Found device: Apple M4 (MoltenVK 0.2.2209) Skipping: Device does not support required feature 'geometryShader' DXVK: No adapters found. Apple GPUs have no geometry shader stage. On an M4, exactly four required features are missing: `geometryShader`, `shaderCullDistance`, `depthClipEnable`, `robustBufferAccess2` + `nullDescriptor`. Side benefit worth noting: with DXVK's dxgi the adapter reports as **Apple M4** (vendor 0x106b). Wine's builtin dxgi reports a fake *Radeon RX 6800*, which pushes games down AMD code paths (MSFS ships amd_ags_x64.dll). 4. **Wine 10 is missing one function.** The game aborts on wine: Call from ... to unimplemented function KERNEL32.dll.WerRegisterCustomMetadata, aborting I diffed all 334 imports of the exe against the 7215 exports of Wine 10's kernel32 + kernelbase: this is the **only** missing one, and it is pure Windows Error Reporting telemetry. Wine 11 (CrossOver 26.3) does implement it, but CrossOver is unusable here because of the MoltenVK version above. Worked around from inside DXVK's dxgi: at DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH it walks the host executable's import table and points that slot at a no-op returning S_OK. Nothing in the game's files is modified. ## How far it got With all four cleared, the sim boots and renders. From its own crash report: BuildVersion="1.8.14.0" GPUName="Apple M4" EnableD3D12=true VideoMemoryBudget = 12.7 GB FrameCount = 55 TimeSpentRunningMs = 3133 Real swapchain at 1470x956 with 3 images, `D32_FLOAT_S8X24_UINT` depth buffer, `R8G8B8A8_UNORM` back buffers, `BC4`/`BC5` textures uploading. It renders **55 frames** of its loading screen. ## Where it dies Stuck at `MainState:BOOT SubState:BOOT_INIT`, black screen with a frozen spinner, always at the same address: wine: Unhandled exception 0x80000003 at 0x143CA82B1 `STATUS_BREAKPOINT` — the game's own assertion. Located via `.pdata`: function at RVA `0x3ca8260-0x3ca82b7` (87 bytes), the `int3` sits at `+0x51`. Depending on timing, Asobo's report says either: Msg="FiberError" Where="HangDetector" Code=0xC0000194 (STATUS_POSSIBLE_DEADLOCK) MSFS rolls **its own fiber system** (`FiberMgr_Z`, `FiberProc`, and an `!!! OUT OF FIBER MEM !!!` string next to `FiberStack`) — hand-rolled coroutines with manual stack switching. It imports no Windows fiber API at all. ## Ruled out, with evidence - **Memory**: 16 GB physical, 5.29 GB free, and a **64 GB contiguous VA reservation** succeeds. Not a memory limit. - **4 KB vs 16 KB pages** (Apple Silicon): Wine reports 4096 and handles it — 4 KB guard pages work, and I created **256 fiber-sized stacks with guard pages** without failure. - **msync**: `WINEMSYNC=0` changes nothing. - **Network**: `lsof` on the process shows zero connections. It is not waiting on Microsoft services. - **VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST**: appears in one run and **not** in another that hangs identically, so it is a consequence (Metal's watchdog killing a stalled command buffer), not the cause. I initially misread this as the root cause. ## What is actually missing Three capabilities Metal does not have, which I had to *fake* to get this far: 1. **`nullDescriptor`** (`VK_EXT_robustness2`). Confirmed in use by the log: `d3d12_desc_create_cbv: Constant buffer desc is NULL`. vkd3d-proton assumes every GPU tolerates null descriptors and writes `VK_NULL_HANDLE`. There is dummy-descriptor infrastructure at `resource.c:9215` but it is **not wired** to this case. This is bounded, real work someone could do. 2. **`robustBufferAccess2`**. 3. **Tiled resources tier 2** — MSFS uses these for terrain. Not a missing implementation; the hardware does not have the feature. This is the one that closes the door. ## Suggested entry Rating 1 for the stock d3dmetal path is the honest primary datapoint. If the DB can carry a note, the SM 6.7 result is the reusable part: it applies to the whole class of DX12 games currently blocked by D3DMetal's 6.6 ceiling, not just this title. Happy to share the patches and the probe sources if useful.
